constraints: The netlist uses a small technology-mapped cell vocabulary including AOI21, OAI22, INV, XOR, and DFF.
The netlist is a flat, gate-level Verilog file.
The control_out signal is a single-bit output of the top-level module.
expected_outputs: A valid trojan_report.json file in the submission directory.
The report must list at least one trigger cell instance and at least one payload cell instance.
The report must list at least one trigger net and at least one payload net.

functional_requirements.requirement: The submitted trojan_report.json must be valid JSON and parseable by a standard JSON parser.
The submitted trojan_report.json must contain the exact top-level keys: "trigger_cells", "trigger_nets", "payload_cells", "payload_nets".
Each of the four required keys must map to a non-empty array of strings.
All reported cell instance names and net names must exist in the provided netlist (design.v).

interface: The participant must produce a single JSON file at submission/trojan_report.json. The file must contain a JSON object with the following required fields: "trigger_cells" (array of strings, instance names of cells implementing the trigger condition), "trigger_nets" (array of strings, names of nets carrying the trigger signal), "payload_cells" (array of strings, instance names of cells implementing the payload), "payload_nets" (array of strings, names of nets carrying the payload effect). All arrays must be non-empty. The evaluator will parse this file and compare its contents against the hidden ground truth.
objective: Analyze the provided gate-level netlist and identify any logic that could cause the control_out signal to flip under a specific, rare input condition. Report the instance names of the cells and nets involved in this behavior.
response_format: A JSON object with keys "trigger_cells", "trigger_nets", "payload_cells", "payload_nets", each mapping to a non-empty array of strings.
